verses.sanskrit:
नारद उवाच।
              बन्धुत्वादथवा सख्याच्छाल्मले नात्र संशयः । पालयत्येव सततं भीमः सर्वत्रगोऽनिलः ॥१॥
verses.english: "Hearing these words of their preceptor, Vyasa's disciples gifted with great energy, became filled with the joy and embraced one another.

verses.sanskrit: न्यग्भावं परमं वायोः शाल्मले त्वमुपागतः । तवाहमस्मीति सदा येन रक्षति मारुतः ॥२॥
verses.english: Addressing one another, these said,-We will remember and act according to what has been said by our illustrious preceptor in view of our future well-being.

verses.sanskrit: न तं पश्याम्यहं वृक्षं पर्वतं वेश्म चेदृशम् । यं न वायुबलाद्भग्नं पृथिव्यामिति मे मतिः ॥३॥
verses.english: Having said this to one another with gladdened hearts, the disciples of Vyasa, who were consummate masters of words, once more addressed their preceptor and said,-If it pleases you, O powerful one we wish to get down from this mountain to the Earth, O great ascetic, for the object of sub-dividing the Vedas.

verses.sanskrit: त्वं पुनः कारणैर्नूनं रक्ष्यसे शाल्मले यथा । वायुना सपरीवारस्तेन तिष्ठस्यसंशयम् ॥४॥
verses.english: Hearing these words of his disciples, the powerful son of Parashara, replied them in these wholesome words which were fraught, besides, with virtue and profit.-You may go to the Earth or to the regions of the gods as ye like. You should always be careful, for the Vedas are such that they are always liable to be misunderstood.

verses.sanskrit: शाल्मलिरुवाच । न मे वायुः सखा ब्रह्मन्न बन्धुर्न च सुहृत् । परमेष्ठी तथा नैव येन रक्षति वाऽनिलः ॥५॥
verses.english: Permitted by their preceptor of truthful speech, the disciples left him after going round him and bowing their heads to him.

verses.sanskrit: मम तेजो बलं भीमं वायोरपि हि नारद । कलामष्टादशीं प्राणैर्न मे प्राप्नोति मारुतः ॥६॥
verses.english: Descending upon the Earth they celebrated the Agnishtoma and other sacrifices; and they began to officiate at the sacrifices of Brahinanas and Kshatriyas and Vaishyas.

verses.sanskrit: आगच्छन्परुषो वायुर्मया विष्टम्भितो बलात् । भञ्जन् द्रुमान् पर्वतांश्च यच्चान्यदपि किंचन ॥७॥
verses.english: Happily spending their days in the domestic mode of life, they were treated by the Brahmanas with great reverence. Possessed of great fame and prosperity, they were engaged in teaching and officiating in sacrifices.

verses.sanskrit: स मया बहुशो भग्नः प्रभञ्जन्वै प्रभञ्जनः । तस्मान्न बिभ्ये देवर्षे क्रुद्धादपि समीरणात् ॥८॥
verses.english: After his disciples had departed, Vyasa remained in his hermitage, with only his son in his company. Passing his days in anxious thoughtfulness, and great Rishi, endued with wisdom, kept silent, sitting in a retired corner of the asylum.

verses.sanskrit:
नारद उवाच।
              शाल्मले विपरीतं ते दर्शनं नात्र संशयः । न हि वायोर्बलेनास्ति भूतं तुल्यबलं क्वचित् ॥९॥
verses.english: At that time Narada of great ascetic merit came there for seeing Vyasa, and addressing him, said these words of sweet sound.

verses.sanskrit: इन्द्रो यमो वैश्रवणो वरुणश्च जलेश्वरः । नैतेऽपि तुल्या मरुतः किं पुनस्त्वं वनस्पते ॥१०॥
verses.english: Narada said O twice-born Rishi of Vashistha's family, why are Vedic sounds silent now? Why are you sitting silent and alone, engaged in meditation like one engrossed in thought?

verses.sanskrit: यच्च किंचिदिह प्राणी चेष्टते शाल्मले भुवि । सर्वत्र भगवान्वायुश्चेष्टाप्राणकरः प्रभुः ॥११॥
verses.english: Alas, destitute of Vedic sound, this mountain has lost its beauty, as the Moon shorn of splendour when possessed by Rahu or covered with dust.

verses.sanskrit: एष चेश्यते सम्यक् प्राणिनः सम्यगायतः । असम्यगायतो भूयश्चेष्टते विकृतं नृषु ॥१२॥
verses.english: Though inhabited by the celestial Rishis, yet shorn of Vedic sounds, the mountain no longer appears beautiful now but resembles a village of Nishadas.

verses.sanskrit: स त्वमेवंविधं वायुं सर्वसत्त्वभृतां वरम् । न पूजयसि पूज्यं तं किमन्यद्बुद्धिलाघवात् ॥१३॥
verses.english: The Rishis, the gods, and the Gandharvas, too, no longer shine as before on account of being deprived of Vedic sound.

verses.sanskrit: असारश्चापि दुर्मेधाः केवलं बहु भाषसे । क्रोधादिभिरवच्छन्नो मिथ्या वदसि शाल्मले ॥१४॥
verses.english: Hearing these words of Narada the Islandborn Krishna answered, saying,-0 Great Rishi, O you who are conversant with the sayings of the Vedas, all that you have said is agreeable to me, and you should say it to me! You are omniscient. You have seen everything. Your curiosity knows all things.

verses.sanskrit: मम रोषः समुत्पन्नस्त्वय्येवं सम्प्रभाषति । ब्रवीम्येष स्वयं वायोस्तव दुर्भाषितं बहु ॥१५॥
verses.english: You know everything in the three words. Do you, then, Otwice-born Rishi, order me.0, tell me what I am to do.

verses.sanskrit: चन्दनैः स्यन्दनैः शालैः सरलैर्देवदारुभिः । वेतसैर्धन्वनैश्चापि ये चान्ये बलवत्तराः ॥१६॥
verses.english: Tell me, O twice-born Rishi, what should now be done by me. Separated from my disciples, my mind has become very dispirited.

verses.sanskrit: तैश्चापि नैवं दुर्बुद्धे क्षिप्तो वायुः कृतात्मभिः । तेऽपि जानन्ति वायोश्च बलमात्मन एव च ॥१७॥
तस्मात्तं वै नमस्यन्ति श्वसनं तरुसत्तमाः ।  त्वं तु मोहान्न जानीषे वायोर्बलमनन्तकम् । एवं तस्माद्गमिष्यामि सकाशं मातरिश्वनः ॥१८॥
verses.english: Narada said The fault of the Vedas is the suspension of their recitation. The fault of the Brahmanas is their non-observance of vows. The Vahika race is the stain of the Earth. Curiosity is the fault of women.
